- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.5), model underestimates; raise forecast by 5–10% to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after sharp price increases.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; adjust final 5–7 days upward if sentiment turns bullish mid-horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with cycle phase; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
